title: In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm (Extended Version)
version: Extended version published 2014-05-20 (USENIX ATC '14 paper plus extra material)
why: The canonical Raft description, whose Section 2 states the replicated state machine problem, Section 5.2 gives leader election with terms and randomized timeouts, and Section 5.6 states the broadcastTime << electionTimeout << MTBF timing requirement.

title: Consensus: Bridging Theory and Practice (PhD dissertation)
version: Stanford University, August 2014; dissertation source commit 0c10ea1b (2016-05-24)
why: Ongaro's full dissertation gives the longer motivation and design rationale behind Raft, with Chapter 3 ('Basic Raft algorithm') covering terms, election rules and split votes, Section 3.8 persisted state and server restarts, and Section 3.9 the timing requirement.

title: Paxos Made Simple
version: 2001-11-01 (SIGACT News 32(4), December 2001)
why: Lamport's own short statement of the consensus problem and its safety conditions (Section 2.1, 'The Problem'), best for showing what any agreement protocol such as Raft must guarantee and how it differs from Paxos.

title: Impossibility of Distributed Consensus with One Faulty Process
version: Journal of the ACM Vol. 32, No. 2, April 1985, pp. 374-382
why: The classic impossibility proof that no deterministic asynchronous protocol can guarantee termination with even one crash-faulty process, which explains why Raft and Paxos give up guaranteed liveness and assume partial synchrony.

title: etcd-io/raft (Go Raft library)
version: tag v3.7.0 (commit b867cf13f6bc0dae21204302df97bc2355c3af55)
why: The most widely deployed Raft implementation, where raft.go holds the follower/candidate/leader state machine, term handling and randomized election timeouts, and the README states exactly which state must be persisted and synced before messages may be sent.

title: fsync(2) - synchronize a file's in-core state with storage device
version: Linux man-pages 6.19-1 (2026-02-08); read locally as 'man 2 fsync'
why: Primary description of what fsync and fdatasync actually guarantee, including that a directory entry needs its own fsync and that some kernels and filesystems do not flush disk caches at all.

title: PostgreSQL 17 Documentation, 28.3. Write-Ahead Logging (WAL)
version: PostgreSQL 17.11 documentation (page dated 2026-08-13)
why: A production database explaining the write-ahead log idea, why only the WAL must be synced to commit a transaction, and how the log is replayed after a crash.

title: Atomic Commit In SQLite
version: sqlite.org/atomiccommit.html, last updated 2026-04-21
why: Step-by-step account of a real journal-based commit, including SQLite's explicit hardware assumptions about sector writes and ordering, best for the durable-vs-volatile state and fsync-ordering part of the bridge chapter.

title: Consensus: Bridging Theory and Practice (PhD dissertation)
version: Stanford University, August 2014; identical PDF read as online.pdf at github.com/ongardie/dissertation (the Stanford URL did not fetch in the scout harness)
why: Longer authoritative treatment of Raft log replication, commitment and the safety proof, with errata and formal-spec appendix the paper lacks.

title: Students' Guide to Raft
why: Checklist of the AppendEntries, nextIndex/matchIndex and commitIndex mistakes MIT 6.824 implementers actually made, including why log[N].term == currentTerm is required.

title: 6.5840 Lecture 6: RSM and Raft (1)
version: 6.5840 (6.824) spring 2026 course notes, Lecture 6
why: Frames the replicated log's purpose and gives a concrete multi-term log-divergence example that motivates the repair and commit rules.

title: 6.5840 Lecture 7: Raft (2)
version: 6.5840 (6.824) spring 2026 course notes, Lecture 7
why: Walks a full log-repair trace and derives the fast conflict-backup scheme (XTerm/XIndex/XLen) plus the two meanings of committed behind Figure 8.

title: etcd raft package: raft.go and log.go
version: etcd v3.5.12 (raft package; read 2026-10-11)
why: Production Go implementation showing handleAppendEntries, maybeAppend/findConflict truncation and the currentTerm check in maybeCommit.

title: raft.tla: TLA+ specification of Raft
version: commit 6ecbdbcf1bcde2910367cdfd67f31b0bae447ddd (2025-02-18); differs slightly from dissertation Appendix B
why: Machine-readable formal spec to check exact AppendEntries, log-append and commit conditions against a real implementation.

title: Raft Refloated: Do We Have Consensus?
version: ACM SIGOPS Operating Systems Review 49(1), January 2015
why: Independent reimplementation that restates the commitment subtlety with its own worked Leader-Completeness violation and reports a livelock caused by that rule.

title: TLA+ specification for the Raft consensus algorithm
version: master branch, raft.tla (repo last pushed 2025-02-18), read 2026-10-11
why: Best for reading the basic algorithm as a machine-checkable state machine, including the history variables used in the safety proof; note that it models the static-configuration algorithm only, not membership changes.

title: etcd-io/raft (Raft library used by etcd)
version: tag v3.7.0
why: Best for seeing both mechanisms as production Go: the vote-time up-to-date comparison (raft.go:1220-1222 calling raftLog.isUpToDate) and joint-consensus configuration bookkeeping (confchange.Changer.EnterJoint at confchange/confchange.go:57 with tracker/quorum).

title: Planning for Change in a Formal Verification of the Raft Consensus Protocol
version: CPP 2016 (5th ACM SIGPLAN Conference on Certified Programs and Proofs), read 2026-10-11
why: Best for the machine-checked counterpart of chapter 7's proof sketch: a Coq/Verdi proof of state machine safety for Raft that had to discover and prove about 90 invariants, which shows where the informal argument is subtle and needs strengthening.

title: etcd documentation: Runtime reconfiguration
version: etcd v3.5 docs, page last modified 2021-10-26
why: Best for the operator-visible rules that follow from chapter 8: change one member at a time, add a member as a learner and promote it only after it has caught up, and the strict-reconfig-check guard against losing quorum during a change.

title: bug in single-server membership changes (raft-dev mailing list)
version: thread started 2015-07-10 by Diego Ongaro, read 2026-10-11 (also listed in the dissertation errata)
why: Best for the correction every reader of the thesis needs: a counterexample where concurrent single-server changes across a term boundary in an even-sized cluster overwrite a committed entry, the scope of the bug, and the fix that a leader may not append a configuration entry until it has committed an entry in its current term.

title: Safety of Raft single-server membership changes (Diego Ongaro gist)
version: gist created 2015-06-22, last updated 2025-04-23, read 2026-10-11
why: Best for the case analysis that carries chapter 7's leader-completeness argument over to membership changes, enumerating the configuration relationships in which the overlapping voter must exist under the patched single-server rule.

title: go.etcd.io/etcd/raft/v3 package documentation (raft/doc.go)
version: etcd v3.5.15 (tagged July 2024)
why: States the library's contract with the caller: the Node.Ready loop, the Storage interface the application must implement, and that transport, persistence and the state machine are left to the caller.

title: etcd/raft Node API: Ready, ReadStates, ReadIndex, ReportSnapshot, ReportUnreachable (raft/node.go)
version: etcd v3.5.15
why: The concrete Go API for linearizable read-index requests, snapshot send/receive acknowledgement, and unreachable-follower reporting needed to run a real Raft node.

title: etcd API guarantees
version: etcd v3.5 docs (page last modified 2025-09-26)
why: The client-facing contract to check implementations against: strict serializability and durability for KV calls, linearizable by default versus stale serializable reads, and watch/lease guarantees.

title: Jepsen: etcd 3.4.3
version: analysis dated 2020-01-30, testing etcd 3.4.3 on five-node clusters
why: A Jepsen fault-injection study of a production Raft system, best for how partition, crash, clock-skew and membership tests are designed and for real stale-read and lock-safety bugs.

title: How TiKV Uses "Lease Read" to Guarantee High Performance, Strong Consistency and Linearizability
version: TiKV blog, 2020-02-27
why: Compares Raft Log Read, ReadIndex Read and Lease Read and documents TiKV's lease-renewal choices, the clearest practical account of linearizable read paths.

title: Finding bugs in Raft implementations
version: Antithesis blog, 2026-07-27 (bugs reported as hashicorp/raft issues 695, 696, 697)
why: Shows deterministic-simulation testing with fault injection and dissects three commonly-hit implementation bugs, including an InstallSnapshot that ignores the paper's rule to discard the log.

title: etcd documentation: FAQ (quorum, membership, failure tolerance)
version: etcd v3.5 docs, page last modified 2024-12-05
why: Operator-facing statements of etcd's quorum arithmetic ((n/2)+1), the majority/failure-tolerance table, the recommendation to run an odd number of members and no more than seven nodes, and the three-node minimum.

title: CS 2620 lecture notes: Fischer-Lynch-Paterson impossibility
version: Harvard CS 2620 lecture notes, page read 2026-10-11
why: A text-readable university lecture note that states the FLP system model and result; S4 (the JACM 1985 paper) is a scanned PDF that yields no text in this harness.

title: PostgreSQL 17 Documentation, 28.1. Reliability
version: PostgreSQL 17.11 documentation (page dated 2026-08-13)
why: Authoritative account of why a partially written page can be repaired from full page images recorded in the WAL and of the CRC-32C protection on every WAL record.

title: ARIES: A Transaction Recovery Method Supporting Fine-Granularity Locking and Partial Rollbacks Using Write-Ahead Logging
version: ACM Transactions on Database Systems 17(1):94-162, March 1992 (PDF read via people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~brewer/cs262/Aries.pdf)
why: The canonical write-ahead-logging recovery algorithm; best for why redo during replay must be idempotent and how the per-page LSN enforces it.
